sources.entry: yabai - Keyboard-driven tiling window manager. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon] ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]](https://github.com/koekeishiya/yabai/wiki)
Yabai - A tiling window manager for macOS based on binary space partitioning.

summary.one_liner: yabai is a tiling window manager for macOS that automatically arranges windows using binary space partitioning and is controlled through a command line interface.
summary.what_it_does: yabai extends the built-in macOS window manager and lets you control windows, spaces, and displays from a command line interface. Its main function is automatic tiling, which rearranges window layouts using a binary space partitioning algorithm. Other listed features include focus-follows-mouse, disabling animations when switching spaces, and creating spaces beyond the 16-space limit. Keyboard shortcuts can be defined with skhd or other third-party software. An optional scripting addition, which requires partially disabling System Integrity Protection, injects into Dock.app to control windows with functions that need elevated privileges.
use_cases: automatic tiling of windows on a Mac
arranging windows across multiple displays and spaces
scripting window layouts from the command line
how_to_run: Follow the installation methods in the yabai wiki (the README links to it and does not list commands)
Grant Accessibility permission when yabai first launches and restart it
Enable 'Displays have separate Spaces' in Mission Control settings
Optionally configure keyboard shortcuts with skhd
Sample configs are in the examples directory of the repository
notable: Command line interface for controlling windows, spaces, and displays
Optional scripting addition injected into Dock.app for privileged window control
Creates spaces beyond the macOS 16-space limit
Supports macOS Big Sur through Tahoe on Intel and Apple Silicon
caveats: Requires Accessibility permission, and some features need Screen Recording permission or partially disabling System Integrity Protection
Several macOS settings must be changed for commands to work reliably, and windows using native macOS tabs (such as Terminal and Finder) behave incorrectly
Building from source requires codesigning the binary; the author disclaims responsibility for any machine damage
